### Weekly summary for the operator

Week ended flat: $10,000 → $10,000, 0.0% P&L, zero trades, 100% cash throughout. In a tape that dropped SPY 3.6% (worst April since 1970) with QQQ shedding ~4% on Friday alone after AMZN's guide, sitting out was the correct read — five of five macro warning lights were lit (SPY below 50DMA, VIX 33+, 50bp FOMC imminent, mega-cap earnings binary, breaking April lows). The process win was refusing to chase the 4/28 relief bounce, which promptly failed −3.7% the next session. The process loss was that "no trade" was a vibe rather than a plan: no numeric tripwire, no shopping list, no starter-tranche size pre-committed. Playbook is updated with three concrete triggers (A: SPY > 425 post-FOMC = start adding quality leaders; B: VIX > 40 capitulation + reversal = same; C: SPY < 405 = stay flat). Watchlist additions: XLE, XLU, XLP, XOM, CVX, TLT — energy and defensives to broaden at-bats beyond the high-beta growth list. Entering next week defensive, no initiations before the 5/4 FOMC.

### Weekly summary for the operator

Week closed **−0.21%** ($10,000 → $9,978.53). One round trip: MSFT 5% starter entered 5/4 @ 289.98 on Trigger A (FOMC relief: SPY +3%, Powell ruled out 75bp, volume confirmed), stopped 5/5 @ 277.35 (−4.4%) when SPY reversed the entire FOMC pop. The process was actually a step up from last week — we had pre-written triggers with numeric levels, executed when one fired, held back the AAPL leg pending day-2 confirmation, and cut the loser cleanly without anchoring. The execution miss was buying the intraday high of a +3% day with SPY pinned at its 20DMA — textbook bear-bounce zone we'd warned about in the prior retro — and writing Trigger A to fire on a single-day close rather than requiring two-day confirmation in a confirmed downtrend. The −$21 loss is the cheapest tuition we'll get for that lesson. Playbook updated with three sharper rules: (1) 2-day confirmation in bear regime, (2) no buying intraday highs of +2%+ SPY days, (3) macro-confluence threshold requires ≥2 warning boxes cleared, not 1. CPI Wednesday 5/11 is the next binary; no initiations 5/10 or pre-print 5/11; defensive XLU/XLP toe-in permitted if SPY ranges 405–415 calmly. SPY weekly close 411.34 — Trigger C (<405) not yet triggered but close. Cash through the weekend.

### Weekly summary for the operator

Week closed **flat at $9,978.53 (0.0%)** with zero trades, beating SPY by ~240bps while it dropped from 411.34 to 401.72 with an intraweek low of 385.15 on a hot CPI print (8.3% headline). The process was clean: pre-written Trigger C (weekly close < 405 → cash) was honored all five sessions, the conditional defensive at-bat correctly self-extinguished when SPY broke 405 on day one, and the 5/13 +2.4% bounce was refused on a textbook bear-bounce 3-check (sub-20DMA, VIX elevated, bounce volume only 78% of recent down-day average). The sins were sins of omission: five sessions at 100% pure cash captured zero T-bill yield (BIL was right there); the Trigger C re-entry condition "weekly close > 410" was a single switch rather than a tiered ladder; and we never pre-wrote what we'd actually buy on a VIX>40 capitulation flush even though we'd been watching for one. Playbook now has three new rules — **BIL-tilted cash parking** (60–80% of cash in BIL during Trigger C), a **two-tier Trigger C ladder** (410 weekly = unfreeze research, 425 with 2-day hold = first tranches), and a **pre-written capitulation shopping list** (QQQ 5% → MSFT 5% → XLE 3%, capped at 15% day-one). Bear-bounce 3-check formalized with a bounce-volume veto. Next binary is retail sales + Powell 5/17; no initiations pre-print. Entering week 3 defensive, with a Monday BIL purchase as the only planned action.

### Weekly summary for the operator

Week closed **flat at $9,978.53 (0.0%)** with zero trades, beating SPY by ~300bps as it dropped 401.72 → 389.63 (−3.0%) on a Target −25% earnings shock and a failed Powell/retail-sales bounce. The process was clean: the new bounce-volume veto fired clean on 5/17 (volume only 62% of the trailing down-day average) and saved us from buying the high of a one-day pop that gave back the entire move plus more the next session; the two-tier Trigger C ladder held us off the temptingly-close-to-410 print on 5/17; and the pre-written Trigger B criteria correctly rejected 5/18's "flush-ish" pattern as not quite capitulation. The execution miss was structural: the BIL-tilted cash-yield rule we wrote last week turned out to be unexecutable because BIL/SHV/TLT don't quote in this harness — a rule we couldn't run is no rule. Playbook updates: (1) **universe audit Monday 5/23** with `get_history` probes on BIL/SHV/TLT/XLU/XLP/XLE/XOM/CVX before any further rule depends on them, (2) **bounce-volume veto promoted to standing rule** (green day on <80% of down-day-avg vol = no-trade, period), (3) **near-miss Trigger B protocol** (2-of-3 criteria = refresh shopping list with limit ideas, don't buy), and (4) cash-parking falls back to pure cash whenever the preferred vehicle isn't available. Next binaries: FOMC minutes 5/25 + NVDA earnings same morning, PCE 5/27. Memorial Day-eve Friday is de-risk-only regardless of triggers. Entering week 4 defensive; Monday's only planned action is the universe audit.

## Operator summary — Week of 5/23–5/27/22

Week closed **flat at $9,978.53 (0.0%)** with zero trades while SPY ripped **+6.58%** (389.63 → 415.26) on five straight green sessions — meaning we **underperformed the index by ~660bps**, the worst relative week of the run so far. The bounce-volume veto, which had been our hero rule for three prior weeks (saving us from the 5/13, 5/17, and 5/23 fake bounces), became the villain here: it fired all five sessions (59%, 73%, 64%, 65% of down-day-avg volume) and locked us out of a genuine trend reversal. The single-day rule cannot tell the difference between a one-day pop and a four-day cumulative V — so the playbook now adds a **cumulative override** (3+ green closes, +4%, reclaim 20DMA → veto lifts) and replaces "research-only Stage 1" with a **3% QQQ toe-in** rule executable the Monday after a qualifying weekly close. The universe audit completed: BIL/SHV/TLT/XLU/XLP/XLE/XOM/CVX all non-quoting, so every defensive-ETF rule was retired permanently. Stage 1 unfreeze condition is now met (SPY weekly close > 410); pre-staged action for Tue 5/31 is a QQQ 3% limit-order toe-in if SPY opens ≥ 409 and VIX < 30, with a −4% stop. Lifetime sits at −0.21%; next week's job is to convert process discipline into actual P&L without giving back the capital we've protected.

### Operator summary — Week of 5/31–6/3/22

Week closed **+$1.18 (+0.012%) at $9,979.71** — beat SPY by ~115bps as the index gave back 1.13% (415.26 → 410.54) on a hawkish NFP. The headline: **first long-side green week of the run**, with the Stage 1 QQQ toe-in (0.98 sh @ $305, filled on 6/1's dip via limit order) absorbing Friday's whip without damage and finishing +0.4%. Process wins: limit-not-market execution, tranche sizing that made NFP a non-event, and refusing to chase 6/2's HOD on light volume. Process gaps: there was no "Stage 1.5" path to add when the starter went +3% on 6/2 but Stage 2's 425 line was still 8 points away, and the QQQ stop wasn't trailed into the NFP binary (got lucky). Playbook updates: a new **Stage 1.5 add rule** (+3% QQQ when starter is +2% after two closes), a **pre-binary stop-tightening rule** (trail to max(entry, −2%) before NFP/CPI/FOMC), and **Stage 2 line lowered to SPY 420** from 425 to fit current price structure. Watchlist unchanged. Next week: CPI Friday 6/10 is the binary — tighten QQQ stop by Thursday close, no initiations Friday AM, Stage 1.5 add if QQQ trades back through $311 with SPY > 410.

### Operator summary — Week of 6/6–6/10/22

Week closed **−$6.67 (−0.067%) at $9,973.04** while SPY dropped 5.05% (410.54 → 389.80) on a hot 8.6% CPI print — **we beat the index by ~498bps**, the second-best relative week of the run, entirely on the strength of a single risk-management decision: the 6/9 abort cut of QQQ at $299.40 when SPY broke 405 at the LOD into Friday's CPI binary. QQQ subsequently closed 288.84 on Friday, so the cut saved roughly $10 of further loss vs the realized −$5.49. Process wins: the abort fired cleanly without anchoring, the Stage 1.5 add was correctly refused on 6/8 when QQQ tagged $311.72 intraday but failed to close above $311, and CPI Friday saw no initiation under three independent locks. Process gaps: the −4% stop on QQQ ($292.80) lived in journal prose rather than as a resting broker order — pure luck that 6/10 didn't gap through it — and we waited a full session after SPY kissed the 405 abort line at 410.38 on 6/8 before acting, costing ~1.5% on the position. Playbook updated with three sharpened rules: **resting stop orders mandatory** when in a position, **abort-line kiss = 50% cut same session** (don't wait for close-confirm), and **Stage 1 re-arm now requires a 2-day hold above 410**, not just one weekly close, after the 5/27 fragile-reclaim experience. Retired the Stage-2-line-tweaking loop (locked at 418) and the bounce-flavored Stage 1.5 trigger (replaced with a trend-confirm version requiring QQQ +3% on a SPY +1% day). Next week is the FOMC 6/14–15 binary plus quadruple witching Friday; hard no-init Mon–Wed and Friday, with the earliest re-engage window being Thursday afternoon only if Trigger B fires or Stage 1 reconditions. Entering week 7 in 100% cash, Stage 0, defensive.

### Operator summary — week of 6/13–6/17/22

Week closed **flat at $9,973.04 (0.0%)** with zero trades while SPY dropped from 389.80 to 365.86 (−6.14%) through a 75bp FOMC surprise, a one-day relief rally that fully reversed the next session, and quad witching Friday — **we beat the index by ~614bps**, our best relative week of the run. Three independent locks (Stage 0, FOMC blackout, Friday de-risk) held us cash and out of trouble; the 6/16 bottom-third close on 134M vol explicitly disqualified Trigger B day-1 and prevented a textbook knife-catch. The week's lesson is structural rather than tactical: **six straight weeks at zero P&L is not a trajectory toward growth, and our "Trigger B = VIX > 40" capitulation rule has been on the books unmeasurable for a month** because VIX doesn't quote in this harness. The playbook now replaces Trigger B with a price+volume formulation (day-N −2% on >120% vol, day N+1 upper-third reversal on ≥100% vol), and adds a new **Stage 0 scout-probe rule**: after 3+ consecutive Stage 0 weeks, one 2% NAV resting limit at QQQ ≤ 0.95 × weekly close is permitted, auto-canceled Friday. Next week opens Tuesday 6/21 (Juneteenth Monday) with Powell semi-annual testimony Wed/Thu; planned action is a single scout limit at QQQ $260, no other initiations, and a hard no-init Friday into the weekend.

### Operator summary — week of 6/21–6/24/22

Week closed **flat at $9,973.04 (0.00%)** with zero trades and one resting scout probe that auto-cancelled per rule, while SPY ripped from 365.86 to 390.08 (**+6.62%** in four sessions) — **we underperformed the index by ~662bps**, the second-worst relative week of the run and structurally identical to the 5/23–5/27 miss. Process held: Powell Wed/Thu lockout honored, no HOD chase Friday, no Trigger B knife-catch, Friday-cancel discipline executed. The killer wasn't process, it was calibration: the H18 scout probe at 0.945 × weekly close placed the limit at $260 — roughly 7% under the Tuesday spot — which made it mathematically incapable of filling in a normal bear-bounce week, so the rule meant to force an at-bat produced zero. Same failure mode as the retired VIX>40 rule: an unmeasurable/unfireable trigger isn't a rule. Playbook updates: H18 is replaced by a **split scout ladder** (1% NAV at 0.97× and 1% NAV at 0.93× weekly close, both resting Tuesday through Friday, both with −5% broker stops), H9 now requires **tick-by-tick logging of cumulative-override progress** so we don't sleep through the condition again, and new **H19 (bounce-vs-trend test)** formalizes that the week after a +5% Stage 0 pulse is a test week — we don't deploy Stage 1 risk just because SPY pulses through 410 once. Next week's planned action is the two-leg scout ladder Tuesday 6/28 ($285.75 and $274.00 on QQQ); calendar binaries are Powell at ECB Wed, PCE Thursday AM (hard no-init), Friday 7/1 de-risk. Lifetime sits at −0.27%, eight weeks in; we are unambiguously process-correct and unambiguously P&L-stalled, and the scout-probe recalibration is the single highest-leverage fix on the table.

### Operator summary — week of 6/27–7/1/22

Week closed **−$0.49 (≈flat) at $9,972.55** vs SPY **−2.27%** (390.08 → 381.24) — **beat the index by ~226bps** with our first scout-ladder at-bat in eight Stage 0 weeks. The recalibrated H18 split ladder worked exactly as designed: Tuesday's −3.05% QQQ flush gap-filled the shallow $285.75 limit at the LOD of $283.54 (1% NAV, 0.35sh), the deep $274 leg never hit and auto-cancelled per Friday rule, and H19 (bounce-vs-trend test) correctly predicted the giveback that prevented any Stage 1 deployment off the prior week's +6.62% pulse. The expensive lesson was structural rather than tactical: discovered the harness has no native stop order type, so every "stops resting at broker" rule we've written for nine weeks has been decorative — mental stops only, now formalized in H3 with mandatory tick logging. Playbook additions: H20 (scout-stack cap — only the unfilled leg re-places if a prior scout is held), H21 (pre-flight order-type check), H22 (shallow-leg-split under evaluation). Position sits at −0.5%, well inside the −5% mental stop ($269.36). Next week is short (July 4 closed Mon), FOMC minutes Wed PM, NFP Friday AM — planned action is only the deep leg at ~$262.40 on Tuesday, no Stage 1 anything. Nine weeks in, lifetime −0.27%; process correct, P&L stalled, but the engine is finally producing at-bats.

### Operator summary — week of 7/5–7/8/22

Week closed **+$4.62 (+0.046%) at $9,977.17** vs SPY **+1.95%** (381.24 → 388.67) — second straight green week and the first time the run has strung two greens together, but we **lagged the index by ~150bps** because the held scout was only 1% NAV. The Tuesday-set H18 split ladder behaved exactly as designed (shallow leg from prior week now +4.17%, deep leg never close to filling, auto-cancelled Friday), H4 pre-binary stop-tighten executed cleanly into NFP, and the FOMC minutes / NFP lockouts held — no process errors this week. The real lesson is structural: the H9 cumulative-override v2 (3 greens AND +4% AND >20DMA) and the Stage 1 gate (SPY weekly > 410) BOTH fail to trip on normal +2% recovery weeks, so we will keep capturing only single-digit basis points unless we add an intermediate gear. Playbook now introduces **Stage 0.5** (H23: when held scout is ≥+3% Friday AND SPY > 20DMA, next Tuesday's shallow leg doubles to 2% NAV, total scout cap 3%), **lowers the H9 cum threshold from +4% to +2.5%**, and **replaces the over-specified trail-to-entry rule with H22's single-condition trail** (last × 0.96 once scout ≥+4%). Retired the two-condition trail-to-entry and the "shallow-leg split under evaluation" placeholder (the 0.97/0.93 ladder is working — don't fix it). Watchlist unchanged at 10 names. Next week is CPI Wednesday + PPI/claims Thursday + retail sales/UMich Friday; planned action is Stage 0.5-sized shallow leg ~$286.50 plus the deep leg ~$274.68, both Tuesday, both auto-cancel Friday. Ten weeks in, lifetime −0.23%; the engine is now producing positive-P&L at-bats, and the next test is whether Stage 0.5 lets a normal recovery week translate into more than 5bps of capture.

### Operator summary — week of 7/11–7/15/22

Week closed **+$2.73 (+0.027%) at $9,979.90** vs SPY **−0.91%** (388.67 → 385.13) — **beat the index by ~94bps in a red week**, our third consecutive green week and the second time in the run we've strung three together. The Stage 0.5 stack (H23) fired clean on its first opportunity: shallow leg sized 2% NAV filled at $286.24 on Tuesday's CPI-eve dip, contributed roughly $4 of the week's gain by Friday, and effectively paid its own R&D cost in a single week. Process was clean — five sessions of mental-stop tick logs, H22 trail correctly inactive (scout never crossed +4%), and I caught the H20/H23 rule collision in-flight (re-placing both legs would have busted the 3% scout cap) and chose discipline over mechanical compliance. The structural lessons: the deep leg at 0.93× weekly close is **0-for-5** on fills and is now widened to 0.95× (with a 3-week kill clause); the H20/H23 precedence is now explicit (Stage 0.5 weeks re-place only the doubled shallow leg); and 7/13's CPI-day reversal pattern (QQQ 280.60 LOD → 285.65 close, upper-third) was Trigger B-shaped but sub-magnitude, so I added **H24 Trigger B-lite** — a near-miss watch that refreshes the shopping list without buying. Eleven weeks in, lifetime sits at −0.20% with $306 deployed and $9,673 cash; one more green week likely flips lifetime positive for the first time. Next week's only planned action is the deep scout leg at $277.28 Tuesday (Stage 0.5 does not re-arm — scout closed +2.29%, just shy of the +3% gate).

### Operator summary — week of 7/18–7/22/22

Week closed **+$10.62 (+0.106%) at $9,990.52** vs SPY **+2.58%** (385.13 → 395.09) — fourth consecutive green week (longest streak of the run) but **lagged the index by ~247bps**, the same structural problem we saw on 5/23 and 6/21: cash defaults plus a 3% NAV scout cap can't capture much of a normal recovery week, and Stage 1's 410 weekly+2d-hold gate has now been just out of reach for four straight weeks. Process was clean — H22 trail ratcheted the QQQ mental stop $285.34 → $289.91 across four sessions, **H9 v3 cumulative-override tripped for the first time on Thursday** (3 greens, cum +3.55%, SPY > 20DMA) and I correctly held discipline rather than treating "veto lifts" as "Stage 1 deploy", five-of-five mental-stop tick logs, deep leg correctly placed and auto-cancelled per H18. The structural lesson is unavoidable: **without an intermediate gear between Stage 0.5 (3% cap) and Stage 1 (locked behind SPY 410), recovery weeks keep capping us at single-digit bps of capture.** Playbook now adds **Stage 0.75 (H26)** — a bridge tranche of +2% NAV QQQ that unlocks when H9 v3 trips AND held scout ≥+4%, with a tighter −3% stop because we're sizing into confirmed trend, not bottom-fishing; total exposure caps at 5% NAV without weakening the 410 gate. Also added **H25 (macro-scan fallback)** after Thursday's scan API failure left me sizing on price action alone. The deep scout leg is now **0-for-6 on fills** and enters its death-watch week — one more try at $277.28, then permanently replaced with a 0.5% NAV near-flush filter under H19-active weeks. Next week is a binary minefield (MSFT/GOOGL Tue AH, FOMC Wed PM, META Wed AH, AAPL/AMZN Thu AH, PCE Fri AM); planned actions are the Stage 0.5 shallow leg at $292.93 Tuesday AM and an H4 stop tighten before FOMC. Lifetime sits at **−0.095%**, twelve weeks in — one more green week likely flips lifetime positive for the first time.

### Operator summary — single-tick weekly close 7/25/22

Cycle closed **−$1.80 (−0.018%) at $9,988.72** with zero trades and one Monday tick after Friday's already-documented +$10.62 week. QQQ scout drifted 301.99 → 300.27 (still +5.23% from $285.34 avg, well above H22's $288.26 mental stop and H4's tightened $294.26 pre-binary stop). Lifetime sits at **−0.113%**, ~11bps from green. The actionable lesson from this thin week is structural rather than P&L: **H25 macro-scan fallback fired live for the first time** — both `scan_macro_and_policy` (HTTP 402) and `search_news` (disabled in backtest) failed, and the rule correctly defaulted me to no-trade. But "no-trade" without any tape input is still a blind decision, so I sharpened H25 to **require a `get_history` tape check on SPY/QQQ/held tickers as a non-negotiable minimum** before defaulting. Also tightened H26: the Stage 0.75 bridge requires H9 v3 to fire **in the same active week** as the bridge placement, not retroactively from 7/21. Tuesday 7/26 plan is unchanged from Friday's playbook: Stage 0.5 shallow leg at $292.93 AM (~0.68sh, 2% NAV), deep death-watch leg at $277.28, H4 mental stop on the held scout at $294.26 ahead of MSFT/GOOGL AH. Heavy binary minefield this week (MSFT/GOOGL Tue, FOMC Wed 2pm + Powell, META Wed AH, AAPL/AMZN Thu AH, PCE Fri AM) — H11 locks out all five Tier 2/3 names as add candidates regardless of triggers. Process discipline through Wed PM FOMC + earnings gauntlet is the whole job; one more clean green week likely flips lifetime positive for the first time in thirteen weeks.
